subject: opposite direction of effectplot() and estimates from fitqtl()

messages.author: 17766938e328dccc
messages.subject: opposite direction of effectplot() and estimates from fitqtl()
parts:
Dear Karl,

When I was plotting effectplot() for each of my QTLs detected from stpwiseqtl(), I found one of them showed the weird pattern: genotype BB group has higher means than AA , while in the fitqtl() using "get.ests=TRUE" I saw the additive effect estimate for the same QTL  was negative. That's not the case for the rest of QTLs. I am guessing effectplot() gives me contrast between genotypes based on that single marker but fitqtl() takes the whole model into consideration (I have 8 QTLs in total). Thus I would believe that QTL has a genative effect. Could you please provide some insights? Thank you in advance!

Best,
Jiayang

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] opposite direction of effectplot() and estimates from fitqtl()
parts:
It seems really strange that the direction of the effect would change
after accounting for 7 other QTL, but I can't offer any explanation
without further details.

karl

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] opposite direction of effectplot() and estimates from fitqtl()
parts:
Because it’s linked to another QTL (6...@54.0), the effect when considered on its own, as in the plots, could be very different than its effect when considered jointly with the linked QTL, as in fitqtl().

karl
